g-presets.body:
- Keys `1`-`8` load presets in synth and drum mode.
- Hold a key for three seconds to save a snapshot to the snapshot folder (named by date).
- `SHIFT` + `1`-`8` opens the preset browser: blue picks the engine, ochre the preset. Your snapshots are in the snapshot folder; recall and rename them with `T1`-`T4` and the encoders.
- `SHIFT` + `T1` changes only the engine; a preset changes all four modules (engine, envelope, FX, lfo).
- Firmware 1.6 added preset folder management on the device.
g-presets.title: Presets and snapshots

g-drum-fades.body: OS 1.6 added drum sampler release, with control over attack, release or both to shape transients and loops. OS 1.7 draws the drum sample fade in and fade out on screen so you can see what you are setting.
g-drum-fades.title: Drum sampler fades and release

g-encoders.body:
The four encoders are colour coded and their job depends on the screen: blue (first parameter), ochre (second), gray (third) and orange (fourth).
- Turn to change a value. Tap an encoder to confirm, return to the default, or zoom/extend where the screen offers it.
- `SHIFT` + encoder = fine tune or the alternate function.
- Experimenting is encouraged: the guide's advice is to try things and see what happens.
g-encoders.title: The four colour encoders

g-resample.body: Press `INPUT` and choose "output to input / resample" (shown with an ear icon). Whatever the OP-1 Field is playing is routed back into the sampler, so you can record your own mix or a processed sound as a brand-new sample.
g-resample.title: Resample the OP-1 Field itself

g-eng-phase.body: Phase encoders: phase shift (blue), distortion amount (ochre), phase filter (gray), phase tilt (orange).
g-eng-phase.title: Phase engine

x-fm-scan.body: On the input screen (`SHIFT` + `INPUT`) with fm radio selected, tap ochre to scan for stations. Turning ochre while sampling the radio changes station mid-sample for collage sounds (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-fm-scan.title: Scan the radio

g-tape-xfade.body: Firmware 1.6 added short, non-destructive crossfades on both sides of an edit after lift and drop, which cuts clicks. Merge drop arrived in firmware 1.5.0. The guide you uploaded predates it, so confirm its key combination with `HELP` in tape mode.
g-tape-xfade.title: Tape crossfades and merge drop

x-tap-tempo.body: Press the tempo key repeatedly in time to set bpm by tapping. From the user guide.
x-tap-tempo.title: Tap tempo

g-eng-dsynth.body: Dsynth encoders: env crossfader (blue), waveform (ochre), envelope (gray), cross modulation (orange). Hold `SHIFT` for oscillator 2: frequency, waveform, envelope, filter cutoff frequency.
g-eng-dsynth.title: Dsynth engine

x-stacked.body: In the drum sampler, hold `SHIFT` and use ochre to switch channels between stereo L+R and stacked A+B, so two kits or layers share the keys (MusicRadar; guide lists stereo L+R / stacking A+B).
x-stacked.title: Stacked A+B drum channels

x-revert.body: `SHIFT` + `SYNTH` (or `SHIFT` + `DRUM` in drum mode) throws away every change to the current sound and reverts to its saved preset. Handy after wild tweaking. From the user guide.
x-revert.title: Undo sound tweaks instantly

g-drum-sampler.body:
Press any key, set the in point (ochre) and out point (gray), then press the same key again to confirm.
- Turn: tuning (blue), in point (ochre), out point (gray), play mode (orange). Tap ochre or gray to zoom; tap again to exit.
- Hold `SHIFT`: direction, panning, attack, gain; fine tuning on blue. Channels can be stereo (L+R) or stacked (A+B).
g-drum-sampler.title: Drum sampler layout

x-pretape-pan.body: Firmware 1.3.2 added pre-tape pan: in tape mode, `SHIFT` + orange sets where the recording lands in the stereo field. Record one mono part hard left and another hard right on the same track (OP Forums).
x-pretape-pan.title: Pre-tape pan doubles your tracks

x-faux-delay.body: Make a short sound (no sustain), add a tremolo lfo with a square shape (`SHIFT` + orange on the tremolo page) and lengthen the release. You get echo-like repeats and keep `T3` free (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-faux-delay.title: Fake delay without the FX slot

x-endless-focus.body: With an endless or pattern drum sequence running, press `SHIFT` + a key to focus edits on that drum sound only (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-endless-focus.title: Edit one drum inside a running sequence

g-tape-edit.body:
- `LIFT` lifts (erases into memory) a take. `DROP` places the last take in memory. `SPLIT` splits a take.
- `SHIFT` + `LIFT` lifts all four tracks inside an active loop. `SHIFT` + `SPLIT` joins two nearby takes.
- `SHIFT` + `RECORD` arms recording. `SHIFT` + `PLAY` plays in reverse. `SHIFT` + `STOP` sets tape grid resolution.
- `SHIFT` + `LEFT` / `RIGHT` jumps between beat markers. Arrows alone rewind and fast-forward.
- Tape encoders: blue scrub (shift: slide a take), ochre loop point, gray tape speed (shift: tape speed %), orange recording level.
- Firmware 1.5 added merge drop and 1.7 added tape undo.
g-tape-edit.title: Tape editing keys

g-eng-voltage.body: Voltage encoders: modulation (blue), ground noise (ochre), phase filter (gray), detune (orange).
g-eng-voltage.title: Voltage engine

g-amp.body:
The amp engine processes an external signal, such as a guitar into line-in or USB audio, through the OP-1 Field's filters and effects before you record it, so you can capture a processed sound instead of a dry one.
- Controls: volume, compression, tone and drive.
- It includes a built-in tuner for tuning an instrument while you play or rehearse.
g-amp.title: Amp engine and tuner (OS 1.6)

x-meter.body: The LED meter on the right edge shows peak level, while the on-screen mixer meters are averaging VU meters. Use the LEDs to judge whether a recording is loud enough (Elektronauts).
x-meter.title: Trust the LED meter

g-output.body: Press `OUTPUT`. `T4` starts a stereo mixdown of everything you do anywhere on the unit, `T2` stops, `T3` prepares another. Recordings are 6-minute audio files you can copy over usb. Choose the radio antenna instead (blue) to transmit what you play over fm; ochre sets the frequency, pick an unused one. The master effect is captured in a mixdown but never recorded to tape.
g-output.title: Output: mixdown and fm transmit

x-lofi-master.body: In the mixer, push drive (gray on `T4` master out) and put punch on the master effect with high power and low punch. Pull back if it gets tiring (community tip from the original OP-1; guide warns drive costs dynamics).
x-lofi-master.title: Squashed lo-fi master

r-170.body: Headline: tape undo. Also: new MIDI controls, system settings moved to COM > T1, MIDI options moved into system settings, MIDI monitor, SPP origin setting, better incoming MIDI transport over BLE, SPP sent when jumping with `SHIFT` + arrows, a new device list with custom icons for Teenage Engineering devices and a popup when connecting to them, metronome aligned to tape, drum sample fade visualised, loop BPM shown on the tape screen with `SHIFT` in free mode, MTP improvements, fixes for pops after looping recording, terminal fx chirp at startup, tape loop jumping and screen lag after recording.
r-170.title: Firmware 1.7.0 (2026-04-29)

g-eng-pulse.body: Pulse encoders: filter (blue), amplitude (ochre), second pulse (gray), modulation (orange).
g-eng-pulse.title: Pulse engine

x-grid.body: `SHIFT` + `STOP` cycles tape grid resolution, which sets what `SHIFT` + arrows jump between. From the user guide.
x-grid.title: Change the tape grid

g-envelope.body:
`T2` in synth mode is an ADSR envelope: attack (blue), decay (ochre), sustain (gray), release (orange). It is the same on every synth engine except amp, where T2 opens a tuner.
Hold `SHIFT` on the envelope screen for the play mode page: play mode (blue), portamento (ochre, glide between notes), bend range (gray), volume (orange). The original OP-1 guide lists the play modes as polyphonic, monophonic, legato and unison; the Field's screen shows POLY by default.
g-envelope.title: Synth envelope (T2)

x-usb-noise.body: Hear whine when plugged into a computer? In the COM screen (`SHIFT` + `OUTPUT`) tap orange to turn usb charging off. From the user guide.
x-usb-noise.title: Kill usb noise

r-16x.body:
- 1.6.0 (2025-12-16): amp synth engine with tuner, multichannel USB audio, random preset generator, tape crossfades after lift and drop, preset browser folder management, count-in recording, drum sampler release, outgoing MIDI clock over BLE, "input signal safety" setting.
- 1.6.2 (Dec 2025): USB audio compatibility patch, tape crossfade refinements.
- 1.6.5 (2025-12-22): multitrack stability fixes for tempo inconsistencies and drops.
- 1.6.7 (2026-01-19): multichannel audio performance, longer preset names, better loop editing precision.
- 1.6.9 (2026-02-23): USB MIDI stability, option to disable count-in, correct input defaults after factory reset.
r-16x.title: Firmware 1.6.x (Dec 2025 to Feb 2026)

g-teboot.body:
te boot: switch off, unplug usb, hold `COM` (the output key) while switching on.
- Firmware update: connect usb-c, press `1`, copy the firmware file to the disk, eject safely, follow the screen.
- Factory reset: press `7`, press the orange knob to confirm, restart and wait. Erases all user data.
g-teboot.title: te boot, firmware update and factory reset

g-synth-mode.body:
In `SYNTH` mode the keyboard plays the current sound.
- `T1` engine (change engine with `SHIFT` + `T1`), `T2` ADSR envelope, `T3` one effect at a time (`SHIFT` + `T3` to change), `T4` LFO (`SHIFT` + `T4` to change type).
- Left and right arrow keys shift the octave while in synth or drum mode.
- A sound is the combination of engine + envelope + effect + LFO, and those four are what a preset stores.
g-synth-mode.title: Synth mode overview

x-gforce.body: Choose the element lfo (`SHIFT` + `T4`) with g-force as the source, and tilt the unit to move a parameter: filter sweeps, pitch wobble, playback speed on a sample (guide feature; uses from the community).
x-gforce.title: Shake the sound with g-force

g-settings.body: `SHIFT` + tempo opens settings: clock (date and time; orange sets the time), system (display brightness and the radio region/country), tuning (global detune in cents and notes). Blue picks the setting, ochre the parameter, gray the value.
g-settings.title: Settings (shift + tempo)

g-tape-record.body:
1. Press `SYNTH` or `DRUM` and pick your sound.
2. Press `TAPE`, then `T1` to `T4` to choose the track to record on.
3. Find an empty spot on the tape and set the record level with the orange encoder.
4. Hold `RECORD` and start playing. Press `STOP` when finished.
5. Rewind with the arrow keys and listen back.
OS 1.6 added an optional count-in before recording starts, and OS 1.6.9 lets you turn the count-in off.
g-tape-record.title: Record to tape

x-chop-stutter.body: Tape trick `6` (chop) repeats a tempo-locked slice. Tap it repeatedly to creep backwards through the tape for granular-style stutters (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-chop-stutter.title: Stutter and creep with chop

g-vocoder.body:
Added in OS 1.4.2. Load the vocoder into any sound slot, pick an input source (microphone, headset, radio or USB) and play the keyboard.
- The input runs through a bank of 20 filters with adjustable bandwidth and formant shift.
- The carrier is a built-in seven-oscillator polyphonic synth.
- Encoders: waveform, formant, bands and dry/wet mix.
g-vocoder.title: Vocoder engine

g-eng-dna.body: Dna encoders: filter (blue), wave number (ochre), wave modifier (gray), noise (orange).
g-eng-dna.title: DNA engine

g-fm.body:
- Receive: choose FM radio as an input source and pick the frequency with the ochre encoder (auto-scan available). Range 87.5 to 108 MHz.
- Transmit: select the antenna as the output destination. Blue goes live, ochre picks and fine-tunes the frequency, gray auto-syncs with a nearby OB-4. Choose an unoccupied frequency. OS 1.3.2 added pre-scan for the best transmit frequencies.
g-fm.title: FM radio: receive and transmit

x-reverse-play.body: `SHIFT` + `PLAY` plays the tape in reverse. Record a part, reverse it, and resample it for reversed textures. From the user guide.
x-reverse-play.title: Play the whole tape backwards

g-eng-drwave.body: Dr wave encoders: tap for pop-ups. Turn: wave type and length (blue), filter (ochre), phase (gray), chorus (orange).
g-eng-drwave.title: Dr wave engine

g-overview.body:
The OP-1 Field is Teenage Engineering's portable synthesizer, sampler and four-track tape workstation. It is organised around four main modes: `SYNTH`, `DRUM`, `TAPE` and `MIXER`.
- Built-in speaker and microphone, a colour LCD, a low-profile keyboard, an accelerometer and gyroscope.
- Rechargeable Li-Ion battery, about 24 hours of use, charged over USB-C.
- Works as a USB-C audio and MIDI interface, and has Bluetooth LE MIDI and an FM radio receiver and transmitter.
- This companion covers the OP-1 Field only, not the original OP-1.
g-overview.title: What the OP-1 Field is

g-tape-undo.body: OS 1.7.0 added tape undo, which the original OP-1 does not have. Press `UNDO` to step back an edit or recording and `REDO` to bring it back. Teenage Engineering described it as a do-over after 15 years without one.
g-tape-undo.title: Tape undo (OS 1.7)

g-sample-mic.body:
1. Select a sampler (synth sampler engine in `SYNTH`, or the drum sampler in `DRUM`).
2. Press `INPUT` (the key with the microphone symbol) and choose the microphone as the source.
3. Set the recording threshold with the gray encoder and input gain with the orange encoder.
4. Hold any keyboard key and make the sound. Release the key when done.
5. Play the keyboard to hear it and trim the start and end with the encoders.
g-sample-mic.title: Sample with the built-in microphone

g-drum-kit.body:
1. Press `DRUM` and load or record a sample.
2. Press any key on the keyboard to start setting the in point for that key.
3. Set the IN point (start of the sound) with the ochre encoder and the OUT point (end) with the gray encoder.
4. Press the same key again to confirm. Playing that key now triggers that slice.
Tap the ochre or gray encoder to zoom for precise in/out points; tap again to leave zoom. You can also set tuning, attack and release, stereo mode, panning, fade and gain.
g-drum-kit.title: Build a drum kit with the drum sampler

g-eng-string.body: String encoders: the guide's table repeats pulse's labels (filter, amplitude, second pulse, modulation), while the screen shows tension, impulse and impulse type. Check the on-screen labels.
g-eng-string.title: String engine

g-input-sources.body:
`INPUT` toggles the selected source on or off or prepares sampling. `SHIFT` + `INPUT` opens input configuration.
Sources: built-in microphone, line-in (3.5 mm, stereo or mono), FM radio, USB audio and output-to-input (resample). Orange sets input gain, gray sets the recording threshold. OS 1.6 added an "input signal safety" system setting.
g-input-sources.title: Input key, sources and settings

g-modes-t1t4.body:
The `T1`, `T2`, `T3` and `T4` keys change meaning with the mode:
- `SYNTH` and `DRUM`: T1 = engine, T2 = envelope, T3 = effect, T4 = LFO.
- `TAPE`: T1 to T4 select tracks 1 to 4.
- `MIXER`: T1 = main mixer, T2 = equaliser, T3 = master effect, T4 = master out.
Always available: `SYNTH`, `DRUM`, `TAPE`, `MIXER`, `RECORD`, `PLAY`, `STOP`, `HELP`, `SHIFT`.
g-modes-t1t4.title: The four modes and what T1 to T4 do

g-usb-audio.body:
The OP-1 Field is a multichannel USB-C audio interface and can also host USB audio devices (class 2.0 devices supported since OS 1.5.6). Choose the mode in system settings:
- 2-channel: stereo only.
- 8-channel: tape tracks 1 to 4.
- 10-channel: main stereo plus tape tracks 1 to 4 (added in OS 1.6), handy for recording stems straight into a DAW.
g-usb-audio.title: USB audio modes

g-tape-basics.body:
Tape is the heart of the OP-1 Field workflow. Each tape has 4 stereo tracks and 6 minutes of recording per track at normal tape speed, and the unit holds 8 tapes.
Four tape styles change the character: Studio 4-track, Vintage 4-track, Porta 4-track and Disk Mini.
Tape records audio, so a take is fixed. Sequencers record notes instead and let you change the sound afterwards.
g-tape-basics.title: Tape mode basics

x-copy-modules.body: On a sound's `T3` or `T4` page, `LIFT` copies that module; switch preset and `DROP` it in to reuse the effect or lfo (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-copy-modules.title: Copy an effect or lfo between sounds

r-173.body: Stability release: fixes a rare freeze during normal operation, a rare spontaneous factory reset and a crash when handling presets. Also fixes audio editor glitches, Fazer rendering problems and a sampling interface conflict.
r-173.title: Firmware 1.7.3 (latest known, 2026-05-26)

g-reset.body: Enter TE BOOT (power off, unplug USB, hold `COM` while powering on), press `7`, then tap the orange encoder to confirm. This erases all user data, so copy your files off first.
g-reset.title: Factory reset

x-drum-clicks.body: If drum slices click, change the slice's play mode (orange in the drum sampler) from hold to trigger. Trimming slices helps a whole kit fit the sample time (Elektronauts).
x-drum-clicks.title: Remove drum sample clicks

x-drop-on-key.body: In the drum sampler, hold a keyboard key and press `DROP` to place lifted audio on that key only (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-drop-on-key.title: Drop a sample onto one key

g-battery.body:
- About 24 hours of use per charge. Charge only through the USB-C port.
- Charge the unit at least every 6 months. If left unused for a long time it may not charge again.
- Only qualified people should replace the battery, and only with a Teenage Engineering battery.
- Working temperature 10 to 35 C (50 to 95 F). Storage 0 to 30 C (32 to 86 F).
- Clean the shell with a lightly damp cloth and let it dry. The soft velcro rings on the underside let you attach it to a case or stand.
g-battery.title: Battery care and operating limits

x-liftall-bounce.body: `SHIFT` + `LIFT` lifts all four tracks inside the active loop. Drop them into the drum or synth sampler to get a mixed bounce that respects your mixer levels, then play or record it to a fresh track. Mute tracks first with `SHIFT` + `T1`-`T4` in the mixer to leave them out (Elektronauts). The bounce-to-sampler part comes from community reports.
x-liftall-bounce.title: Bounce all four tracks (lift all)

x-sound-path.body: `SHIFT` + `MIXER` opens the sound path. A warning symbol lights up wherever a critical level is set to zero, the quickest way to find why something is silent (user guide).
x-sound-path.title: Find silent tracks fast

g-eng-cluster.body: Cluster encoders: wave number (blue), wave envelope (ochre), spread (gray), unitor (orange).
g-eng-cluster.title: Cluster engine

x-memo.body: In tape mode, hold `7` or `8` while turning encoders to memorize parameter changes, then tap to jump back to them. Community reports say memos store differences rather than absolute values, and pressing both combines them (original OP-1 tips).
x-memo.title: Memo 1 and memo 2 for performance moves

g-sampler-engine.body:
A chromatic stereo sampler with region looping. Playing a key plays from the start point, loops a section if enabled, and plays to the end on release.
- Turn: start (blue), loop in (ochre), loop out (gray), end (orange). Tap any encoder to zoom in around that point; tap again to exit.
- Hold `SHIFT`: direction, fine tune (finer tune when zoomed), loop fade, gain.
- The envelope (`T2`), effect (`T3`) and lfo (`T4`) still apply.
g-sampler-engine.title: Synth sampler engine

g-bluetooth.body: Turn on Bluetooth MIDI advertising with the blue encoder on the COM screen so other devices can pair. OS 1.6 added outgoing MIDI clock over Bluetooth LE, and OS 1.7 improved incoming transport over BLE, added a MIDI monitor to system settings, an SPP origin setting, and sends song position pointer when you jump with `SHIFT` + arrows.
g-bluetooth.title: Bluetooth MIDI

x-nudge.body: On the tempo screen, the left and right arrows nudge the tempo, so you can stay with another player without sync. Guide pro-tip.
x-nudge.title: Nudge tempo when jamming

x-detune-warmth.body: `SHIFT` + tempo, then tuning, sets a global detune in cents. Record a part, detune a few cents, and record it again on another track for a chorus-like spread (guide setting; technique from the community).
x-detune-warmth.title: Warm up doubled parts with tuning

g-drum-playmode.body:
In the drum sampler (`DRUM` then `T1`), each key has its own settings. Orange sets that key's play mode, which decides whether a hit plays its whole slice or follows how long the key or a sequencer note is held. The Field guide labels the knob without listing options; the original OP-1 guide lists play to end, loop and play once. Shifted: direction (blue), panning (ochre), attack (gray), gain (orange).
The step sequencers (pattern, finger, endless) have no per-step gate length; only the arpeggio has a note length (`SHIFT` + blue). To cut long drum hits short, use the drum envelope (`T2`): lower release (gray) and timing (orange).
g-drum-playmode.title: Drum sampler play mode and gating hits

r-13x.body:
- 1.3.2 (2022-11-17): keyboard velocity sensitivity, mono/stereo setting for line-in, pre-tape pan, WAV import over MTP, pre-scan for the best FM transmit frequencies, tape speed follows external clock, transmit frequency sync with OB-4, finger sequencer velocity, arpeggio "each" bug fix, lift/drop crash fixes.
- 1.3.7 (2022-12-19): crash fixes for patch switching and tape operations.
r-13x.title: Firmware 1.3.x

g-fx-terminal.body: Added in OS 1.5 (December 2023). A bit-crusher and sample-rate reducer with a filter for crunchy lo-fi sound. Encoders: frequency / sample rate (blue, about 100 Hz to 20 kHz), bits (ochre, 2 to 16), model (gray, a resonant band-pass filter that shapes the aliasing), mix (orange, dry to wet). Pick it with `SHIFT` + `T3`. On screen it is drawn as a vintage computer: incoming audio scrolls as a green data stream and played notes light up on the computer's keyboard.
g-fx-terminal.title: Terminal effect

g-tape-speed.body:
- Gray encoder controls tape speed, linked to BPM through the Link setting. With MIDI clock enabled and the link on, tape speed follows the external clock.
- OS 1.7 can align the metronome to the tape, and holding `SHIFT` on the tape screen in free mode shows the loop BPM.
- Orange toggles the metronome and sets its sound and level.
g-tape-speed.title: Tape speed, loop BPM and the metronome

g-fx-list.body:
Press `T3` for the effect, `SHIFT` + `T3` to pick another (blue scrolls, `T3` confirms). Press `T3` again to toggle it. One effect per sound, plus one master effect in mixer `T3`. Guide effects (blue / ochre / gray / orange):
- cwo: frequency, delay, feedback, sideband.
- delay: range, speed, feedback, level.
- grid: x size, y size, z feedback, mix.
- mother (reverb): distance, gate, color, mix.
- nitro: frequency, filter follow, feedback, frequency.
- phone: tone, gsm, baud, telemetry.
- punch: frequency, punch, rounds, power.
- spring: tone, turns, damping, mix.
Firmware 1.5 added the terminal effect.
g-fx-list.title: Effects list and parameters

x-tape-artifacts.body: While recording, nudge blue (scrub) a click or two left or right, or slow tape speed (gray on the tempo screen) after recording for a mellow, pitched-down feel (community tips from the original OP-1).
x-tape-artifacts.title: Tape wobble on purpose

x-instant-stop.body: Pressing tape trick `4` (break) together with `5` (reverse) stops the tape instantly with no slowdown (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-instant-stop.title: Instant tape stop

x-mic-texture.body: Gently blow on or rub the built-in mic while recording through a big reverb (mother) for atmospheric layers (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-mic-texture.title: Mic soundscapes

r-15x.body:
- 1.5.0 (2023-12-15): new terminal effect, tape merge drop.
- 1.5.6 and 1.5.7 (2024): USB audio class 2.0 support, selectable input channels, enumeration improvements.
- 1.4.2 (2023-01-12): vocoder synth engine, start armed tape recording on external MIDI, AIFF and AIFC files for patches over MTP.
- 1.4.5: external clock sync bug fixes. 1.4.7: velocity handling and visual fixes.
r-15x.title: Firmware 1.5.x and 1.4.x

g-dbox.body: Dbox is a two-oscillator drum synthesiser. Each keyboard key is a different sound. Hold `SHIFT` to reach the second oscillator layer. Adjust pitch, waveform, envelope, cross modulation and filter cutoff per oscillator.
g-dbox.title: Dbox drum synth

g-com.body: `SHIFT` + `OUTPUT` opens COM: `T1` midi (blue channel, ochre clock, gray notes, orange other midi), `T2` ctrl (OP-1 Field as a midi controller: channel, relative/absolute encoders, octave), `T3` list (usb and bluetooth midi devices), `T4` mtp (hold `SHIFT` and press `T4` for disk mode). Tap blue to advertise bluetooth midi. Tap orange to toggle usb charging, which can remove usb noise. Press `SHIFT` + `COM` again to return. Firmware 1.7 moved system settings to COM > T1.
g-com.title: The COM screen

g-eng-dimension.body: Dimension encoders: waveform (blue), modulation (ochre), filter cutoff frequency (gray), filter resonance (orange).
g-eng-dimension.title: Dimension engine

g-eng-fm.body: Fm encoders: tap for pop-ups. Turn: fm amount (blue), frequency (ochre), topology (gray), detune (orange).
g-eng-fm.title: Fm engine

g-sample-line.body:
1. Plug the source into the 3.5 mm audio input.
2. Press `INPUT` and choose "built-in microphone / line in".
3. Switch stereo or mono with the ochre encoder (a mono/stereo setting for line-in arrived in OS 1.3.2).
4. Set gain (orange) and threshold (gray), then hold a key to record into the sampler and trim as usual.
Sampling time per sample is limited; trim and re-sample for longer material.
g-sample-line.title: Sample from line-in

x-master-fx-mixdown.body: The master effect (mixer `T3`) is never recorded to tape, but it is captured in an output mixdown. Bounce with output if you want it baked in (user guide).
x-master-fx-mixdown.title: Master FX only in mixdown

g-mixdown.body:
1. Press `OUTPUT`.
2. Press `T4` to start recording the mixdown, then play anywhere on the OP-1 Field: it captures what you do.
3. Press `T2` to stop. Press `T3` to prepare another recording.
Each recording is a stereo audio file up to 6 minutes long. Connect over USB to copy the files to a computer.
g-mixdown.title: Record a mixdown

x-help-combo.body: Hold `HELP` and press any other key to see information about that key's topic (user guide).
x-help-combo.title: Help on any key

g-mixer.body:
`MIXER` combines the four tape tracks into the stereo output.
- `T1` main mixer: track levels and panning; `SHIFT` + `T1` to `T4` mutes tracks.
- `T2` equaliser: three bands (low, mid, high), each switchable.
- `T3` master effect: one effect on the whole mix.
- `T4` master out: master volume, stereo balance, drive and drive release. Drive narrows the dynamic range and distorts at high levels; the release time sets how much it pumps.
g-mixer.title: Mixer mode

x-arm.body: `SHIFT` + `RECORD` arms the tape. You can then change sounds or screens and start recording exactly when you press `PLAY`. Guide feature; the play-to-start behaviour is from the community tips list.
x-arm.title: Arm recording, then start with play

g-files.body:
1. Connect USB-C to your computer.
2. Press `SHIFT` + `COM`, then `T4` for MTP (the default). Files show up through the Media Transfer Protocol; you can import sounds and export presets. OS 1.7 improved MTP for tape files and UTF-8 names.
3. Disk mode: hold `SHIFT` + `COM`, keep holding `SHIFT` and press `T4`. The OP-1 Field appears as a drive; snapshots are in "snapshot" folders. Always eject before unplugging.
You can import WAV files over MTP (since OS 1.3.2), and AIFF or AIFC files for patches (OS 1.4.2). Mixdown files are also reachable this way.
g-files.title: Move files over USB (MTP and disk mode)

g-tape-tricks.body: In tape (and mixer) mode keys 1-8 are tape tricks: `1` loop in, `2` loop out, `3` loop on/off, `4` break (stops the tape), `5` reverse, `6` chop (tempo-locked repeat), `7` memo 1, `8` memo 2 (memorize any parameters).
g-tape-tricks.title: Tape tricks (keys 1 to 8)

g-sound-files.body:
- Hold a sound key `1`-`8` for three seconds to save a snapshot to the snapshot folder (named by date). Browse them with `SHIFT` + `1`-`8`.
- Save a sound to tape: `LIFT` in synth or drum mode, go to tape, find empty space, `DROP`. Recall it: `LIFT` on tape, switch to synth or drum, `DROP`.
- Disk mode gives access to patch data; snapshots are stored as audio files in the snapshot folders for synth and drum.
g-sound-files.title: Snapshots and saving sounds

g-trouble.body:
- Noise when plugged into USB: toggle USB charging off on the COM screen with the orange encoder.
- Not charging: use only the USB-C charging port; leave a long-unused unit connected for a while.
- Accidental power-offs: set Power Off to "delayed" in system settings.
- Odd behaviour after a long run: OS 1.7.3 fixed a rare freeze and a rare spontaneous factory reset, so update.
- Stuck or corrupted: TE BOOT (hold `COM` at power-on) lets you reinstall firmware or factory reset.
g-trouble.title: Troubleshooting quick list

x-join.body: `SHIFT` + `SPLIT` joins two nearby takes into one, useful before lifting a phrase as one piece. From the user guide.
x-join.title: Glue takes back together

x-ffwd-fast.body: Hold an arrow and press `PLAY` to wind faster than normal. `STOP` + an arrow jumps to the start or end of the tape (Loopy Pro forum, OP-1 Field owner).
x-ffwd-fast.title: Faster winding and jump to ends

g-tape-browser.body: `SHIFT` + `TAPE` opens the tape browser: blue picks tape style, ochre picks the tape; tap blue rename, tap ochre load, tap gray new, tap orange erase/delete. Styles: studio 4-track (15 ips, cleanest), vintage 4-track (7.5 ips), porta 4-track (3.75 ips cassette), disc mini (magneto-optical, compressed). Up to 8 tapes, 6 minutes and 4 stereo tracks each.
g-tape-browser.title: Tape browser and tape styles

x-tombola-play.body: With tombola running, hold `SHIFT` to play the keyboard live while the sequencer holds its notes (community tip from the original OP-1).
x-tombola-play.title: Play over tombola

g-randomize.body: Firmware 1.6 added a random preset generator that reshuffles values while keeping the preset's structure, aiming for musical results. The key combination is not in the guide you uploaded, so check `HELP` on the preset screen. An earlier note here claimed `SHIFT` + `DROP`; that came from an unreliable summary and has been removed.
g-randomize.title: Randomise a preset

g-update.body:
Easy way: connect USB-C and use the web updater at teenage.engineering/apps/update.
Manual way: power off, unplug USB, hold `COM` while powering on to enter TE BOOT, press `1`, copy the .tfw firmware file onto the disk that appears, then eject safely.
g-update.title: Update the firmware

g-engines.body:
Engines in the user guide: cluster, digital, dimension, dna, dr wave, dsynth, fm, phase, pulse, sampler, string and voltage. Firmware added vocoder (1.4.2) and amp with tuner (1.6).
Change the engine only with `SHIFT` + `T1`: turn blue to scroll, press `T1` or tap blue to confirm. `SHIFT` + `1`-`8` changes the whole preset (engine, envelope, FX and lfo).
g-engines.title: Synth engine list

g-power.body:
- Power switch is on the right side. Flip it up: you see the logo and firmware version, then the tape screen.
- Everything saves automatically. There is no manual save.
- First charge: connect USB-C to a computer or charger and leave it until full. A charging LED on the right side shows status.
- Register the unit at teenage.engineering/register.
- Tip from the guide: set Power Off to "delayed" in system settings so you do not switch off by accident.
g-power.title: Power on, saving and first charge

g-help.body:
- Press `HELP` alone for a quick overlay about the current screen.
- `SHIFT` + `HELP` opens the full built-in user guide with the quick-start tutorial. Navigate it with `T1` to `T4` and the encoders.
- Hold `HELP` to show the battery level on the LEDs.
g-help.title: Built-in help, shortcuts and battery check

x-sample-limit.body: Users report a limit of about 500 custom samples or presets; past that, new ones stop showing up on the unit (Elektronauts).
x-sample-limit.title: User sample limit

g-drum-mode.body:
Press `DRUM`. Load kits with `SHIFT` + `1` to `8`; use the encoders to scroll and confirm.
- Drum: a stereo sampler. Assign a slice of a sample to each key by setting in and out points.
- Dbox: a dual-oscillator drum synthesiser where every key is its own sound.
The drum envelope (`T2`) is a transient processor (attack sharpness, release tail, gain, timing), not a normal ADSR.
g-drum-mode.title: Drum mode and the two drum engines

g-lfo.body:
`T4` shows the lfo, `T4` again toggles it, `SHIFT` + `T4` picks the type:
- random: speed, amount, destination, parameter.
- element: an outside source moves a parameter. Sources: external input (mic, line, radio, usb, set on `SHIFT` + `INPUT`), g-force (tilt the unit), envelope (T2), sum (whatever goes to main out). Destinations: synth engine, envelope, FX, main.
- midi: midi CC 1-4 from outside mapped to four internal parameters.
- tremolo: speed (blue), pitch amount (ochre), volume level (gray), envelope (orange). `SHIFT` + blue fine speed; `SHIFT` + orange shape: sine, saw, exp, square, blip. Values can go negative to invert.
- value: speed, amount, destination, parameter. Tap blue for shape: square, ramp, saw, sine. Can be note-synced or free running.
- velocity: keyboard velocity as modulation; destination amount, volume amount, destination, parameter.
g-lfo.title: LFO types

g-tempo.body: Press the tempo (metronome) key. Blue sets bpm (`SHIFT` for fine), press tempo repeatedly to tap tempo. Ochre sets sync mode: free (internal, no sync), beat match (internal clock sync), midi sync (external clock), PO sync. `SHIFT` + ochre in PO sync gives 1/16 sync for modular gear. Gray sets tape speed; link shows if bpm and tape speed are linked. Orange controls the metronome. In PO sync the output splits into dual mono: left is the sync signal, right the audio mix. Arrows nudge tempo when jamming unsynced.
g-tempo.title: Tempo screen and sync

g-seq.body:
`SEQUENCER` toggles; `SHIFT` + `SEQUENCER` opens the browser (blue to choose, tap blue or press `SEQUENCER` to enable). Shifted parameters are after the slash.
- arpeggio: note value, trigger mode, trigger pattern, hold / note length, type, pause-skip, swing.
- endless: note value, swing, trigger pattern, hold / manual mode, rotate pattern, direction.
- finger and finger (drum): move cursor, swing, pattern length, hold / erase notes, play mode.
- hold: break point, mono/poly, transpose, hold (tap for clear).
- pattern: move cursor, swing, pattern length, hold / erase notes, offset notes, move section, play mode.
- sketch: draw x, draw y, move x, move y / erase, use divider, use grid, hold.
- tombola: rotation speed, heaviness, shape, bounciness / manual mode.
g-seq.title: Sequencers and their encoders

g-specs.body:
- Line input: 13 kOhm impedance, 0 to 31 dB analogue gain, max 8 dBu, 98 dBA signal to noise.
- Output: max 8 dBu, 124 dBA signal to noise.
- Bluetooth LE 2402 to 2480 MHz. FM radio 87.5 to 108 MHz (receiver and transmitter).
- Works alongside the TX-6, TP-7, CM-15 and OP-XY in the Field system, and syncs with Pocket Operators and the OB-4 magic radio.
g-specs.title: Audio and wireless specs

g-eng-digital.body: Digital encoders: tap any encoder for a pop-up. Turn: wave shaper (blue), octave (ochre), detune and ring modulation (gray), digitalness (orange).

modes.tape: Lifts (cuts) the take under the playhead on the selected track.

lift.name: lift key
lift.summary: Lift / erase. Picks up a take from tape, or a sound or module, into memory.

combos.does: quick help overlay for the current screen
built-in user guide with a quick start tutorial (navigate with T1-T4 and the encoders)
show battery level on the level meter LEDs
combine help with any other key to see more about that topic

modes.any: Press for quick help. Shift + help opens the built-in user guide. Hold help to show the battery level on the LEDs.

help.name: help key
help.summary: The speech-bubble key. Press for a quick help overlay on the current screen.

combos.does: open the lfo list: random, element, midi, tremolo, value, velocity
toggle the lfo on or off
mute or unmute track 4
in the COM screen: mtp file transfer with a computer
disk mode instead of mtp (hold shift and press T4). Always eject before unplugging

modes.drum: Shows the lfo, same as synth mode.
modes.mixer: Master out: master left (blue), master right (ochre), drive (gray), drive release (orange). Shift links stereo.
modes.synth: Shows the lfo. Press T4 again to toggle the lfo on or off.
modes.tape: Selects track 4.

t4.name: T4
t4.summary: Fourth module key. Synth or drum: the lfo. Tape: track 4. Mixer: master out.

combos.does: rewind
octave down
jump left to the previous beat marker

modes.drum: Shifts the keyboard an octave down.
modes.synth: Shifts the keyboard an octave down.
modes.tape: Rewinds the tape.

left.name: left arrow
left.summary: Rewind. Also octave down in synth and drum, and tempo nudge on the tempo screen.

combos.does: open the effect list (blue scrolls, press T3 to choose)
toggle the effect on or off
mute or unmute track 3
in the COM screen: list and control connected usb and bluetooth midi devices

modes.drum: Shows the effect, same as synth mode.
modes.mixer: Master effect on the main mix. It is not recorded to tape, but it is captured in an output mixdown.
modes.synth: Shows the effect. One effect at a time. Press T3 again to toggle the effect on or off.
modes.tape: Selects track 3.

t3.name: T3
t3.summary: Third module key. Synth or drum: the effect. Tape: track 3. Mixer: master effect.

combos.does: toggle input on or off, or prepare to sample in the sampler
input screen: blue source, ochre fm frequency (tap ochre to scan), gray threshold, orange gain

modes.any: Press to toggle the selected input source, or to prepare sampling when a sampler is selected. Sources: built-in mic / line in, fm radio, usb audio, output to input (resample, the ear).

input.name: input key
input.summary: The microphone key at top right. Records external audio or resamples internally.

combos.does: open the tempo screen
press repeatedly to tap tempo
settings: clock (date and time), system (display brightness, radio region), tuning (global detune)
nudge tempo slower (handy when jamming with others, unsynced)
nudge tempo faster

modes.any: Blue: bpm (shift for fine). Ochre: sync mode (free, beat match, midi sync, PO sync; shift + ochre for 1/16 sync). Gray: tape speed. Orange: metronome level; metronome sound selectable. Link shows whether bpm and tape speed are linked.

tempo.name: tempo key
tempo.summary: Metronome key. Sets master tempo for sequencers, synced lfos and the tape, plus sync mode and the metronome.
